summary: Best-of-N answer-simulation value selector, champion adapter
hypothesis: Generating multiple candidate question sets and selecting the one with the most plan-altering, decision-critical questions should surface higher-value outputs than a single greedy pass, because answer simulation lets us score each set by its practical impact before committing.
technique: A best-of-N ensemble using the champion LoRA adapter produces N candidate question sets (greedy floor included); a deterministic Swift selector then picks the set whose questions best simulate plan-altering, decision-critical answers — testing whether value-oriented selection improves over the adapter alone.
result: Scored 0.383 on the full-30 gate (2 wins / 3 ties / 24 losses vs Sonnet); rubric showed atom=4, spec=3, cover=3, nat=4, nonRed=3 — coverage and spec remained the limiting dimensions, meaning the value-selection signal did not translate into meaningfully better sets over the champion adapter baseline. Discarded.
